subject: AMOVA on SNP file in .txt format

messages.author: 868548b0a976c718
messages.subject: AMOVA on SNP file in .txt format
parts:
Hi,
I'm searching to perform AMOVA on my dataset. But I have an error message that I don't know how eliminate it.
I have 252 genotypes and more than 18000 polymorfic SNPs. To facilitate the calculation I took only the first 100 markers.
These are my command lines:

file <- read.table("trial.txt", header=T)

tfile <- t(file[,1:ncol(file)])   #transpose table
colnames(tfile) = tfile[1, ]   #markers labels
tfile = tfile[-1, ]

# to change rownames because the transposition don't leave the labels "ID"
g <- tfile
ID <- rownames(g)
rownames(g) <- NULL
fx <- cbind(ID,g)
View(fx)

x <- as.data.frame(fx, header=T) #trasform into a data.frame

locs <- x[, -c(1, 2)]
colnames(locs) <- gsub("\\-", "_", colnames(locs))

ind <- as.character(file$lines)     # labels of the individuals
population <- as.character(file$Pop)    # labels of the populations

id <- read.table("strata.txt", header=T)    # add strata

file_genind <- df2genind(locs, ploidy = 2, ind.names = ind, pop = population, strata = id, NA.char = "NA", type = "codom", sep = "") # conversion into a genind object

file_amova <- poppr.amova(file_genind, ~rep/year/plot)
Found 238 missing values.

3 loci contained missing values greater than 5%

Removing 3 loci: JHI_Hv50k_2016_206330, JHI_Hv50k_2016_206596, JHI_Hv50k_2016_20687
Error in if (any (as.numeric (unlist (x @all.names, use.names = FALSE)) ==:
   Missing value where TRUE / FALSE is needed
Additionally: Warning message:
In get_local_ploidy (x): NAs generated by transformation


Someone is able to help me, please?
Thanks,

Antonia

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] AMOVA on SNP file in .txt format
parts:
Hello,

This is a bug in poppr. Thank you for providing a reproducible example. I've created an issue that you can use to track the status of the bug here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/190. It should be fixed within the hour and you can install the new version from github if you have a C compiler.

That being said, since you have 18K markers that appear to be bi-allelic, you may want to consider using the "genlight" object to store your data for this analysis. Details about that object type can be found in the "genomics" tutorial from adegenet: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials 

Hope that helps,
Zhian
